executive_summary: The shop's resilience is compromised by several critical weaknesses. A hidden dependency links astronomy-db to checkout, causing checkout failures whenever astronomy-db is delayed. Core caches and services (valkey-cart, flagd, cart) act as single points of failure, each crashing and halting cart operations with no fallback. Additionally, product-catalog delays have a wide blast radius, degrading all primary journeys. Addressing these hidden couplings, adding redundancy, and isolating blast zones are top priorities to improve the overall score.

weaknesses.title: Hidden checkout dependency via astronomy-db
weaknesses.explanation: Delays on astronomy-db unexpectedly degrade checkout journeys, revealing a hidden coupling not captured in the service map. This can cause checkout latency spikes and aborts when astronomy-db is slow, threatening revenue flow.
weaknesses.evidence: exp-143142-3011, exp-163723-5939, exp-141736-9801, exp-165933-0066 all show checkout p95 >800ms and degraded checkout despite not being predicted.

fix.fix_title: Add circuit breaker & cache for astronomy-db calls
fix.steps: In the checkout service, wrap all calls to astronomy-db with a circuit-breaker library (e.g., resilience4j). Configure a 100 ms timeout, open the circuit after 3 failures, and provide a fallback that returns cached astronomy data populated at startup and refreshed asynchronously. Log circuit state changes for observability.
fix.expected_effect: Checkout latency stays below p95 threshold even when astronomy-db is delayed; aborts are avoided and revenue flow is protected.

weaknesses.title: Single point of failure: valkey-cart
weaknesses.explanation: A crash of valkey-cart aborts all cart journeys with impact 1.00 but affects only the cart (breadth 0.25), showing no fallback or redundancy for the core cart cache.
weaknesses.evidence: exp-104221-fd4f crash on valkey-cart caused cart p95 3007ms, degraded cart only, breadth 0.25.

fix.fix_title: Enable restart policy for valkey-cart and add in-process fallback
fix.steps: Edit docker-compose.yml to add restart: unless-stopped for valkey-cart. In the cart service, add a lightweight in-memory cache that is used when Redis is unavailable, populated from Redis on successful connections. This provides continuity until Redis restarts.
fix.expected_effect: A valkey-cart crash triggers automatic container restart; cart requests fall back to in-process cache, preventing total cart outage.

weaknesses.title: Single point of failure: flagd with hidden cart dependency
weaknesses.explanation: Flagd crash aborts cart journeys, indicating an undocumented dependency of the cart on flagd. No other journeys are affected, exposing a fragile link in the checkout path.
weaknesses.evidence: exp-141616-6842 crash on flagd caused cart p95 3051ms, degraded cart only, breadth 0.25, hidden dependency on cart.

fix.fix_title: Circuit-break flagd calls in cart service
fix.steps: Introduce a circuit-breaker around every flagd request in the cart service (e.g., using opossum). Set a 50 ms timeout and a fallback that returns default flag values. Record metrics for circuit state to aid debugging.
fix.expected_effect: Cart journeys continue with sensible defaults when flagd crashes, eliminating the hidden dependency impact.

weaknesses.title: Single point of failure: cart service
weaknesses.explanation: The cart service crash directly aborts cart journeys with impact 1.00 and breadth 0.25, confirming the cart as a critical single point without automatic failover.
weaknesses.evidence: exp-142250-d200 crash on cart caused cart p95 3007ms, degraded cart only, breadth 0.25.

fix.fix_title: Add restart policy for cart service
fix.steps: Update docker-compose.yml to set restart: unless-stopped for the cart service. Optionally define modest CPU/memory limits under deploy.resources to keep the container lightweight. This ensures the cart container is automatically relaunched after a crash.
fix.expected_effect: Cart service recovers automatically after a crash, reducing downtime and keeping cart journeys available.

weaknesses.title: Wide blast radius: product-catalog delays
weaknesses.explanation: A 300 ms delay on product-catalog triggers watchdog breaches across cart, checkout, home, and product journeys, degrading all major user flows and showing a large blast radius.
weaknesses.evidence: exp-164224-dcfe delay 300ms on product-catalog caused product p95 1226ms, cart p95 1250ms, degraded cart,checkout,home,product, breadth 1.00.

fix.fix_title: Timeout, retries and caching for product-catalog calls
fix.steps: Wrap product-catalog client calls in all dependent services with a wrapper that enforces a 200 ms timeout, performs up to 2 retries with exponential backoff, and caches successful responses for 5 minutes. Use a library like axios-retry or similar. Log retry attempts and cache hits.
fix.expected_effect: Downstream services tolerate product-catalog latency spikes, preventing watchdog breaches and limiting blast radius across all journeys.

formula: penalty = 100 x (0.5 x impact + 0.3 x breadth + 0.2 x recovery); service score = 100 - worst penalty on that service; overall = mean of service scores weighted by the number of journeys the service sits on (at least 1; the larger of the map's count and the journeys it was seen to degrade). An experiment whose recovery was not measured (operator stop) contributes no recovery component.
methodology: An independent synthetic prober exercises four user journeys (home, product, cart, checkout) through the front proxy every second. It is the ground truth and does not depend on the application's own telemetry.

A baseline run fixes per-journey error rate and p95 latency and derives safety thresholds from them. A watchdog aborts any experiment that breaches a threshold or loses sight of the prober. Before injection, the safety agent reviews the plan against the baseline limits, recent outcomes and the learned limits, and may approve it, reduce its intensity or veto it; it can never raise an intensity. The planner remembers, across runs, the lowest intensity per target and fault kind that the watchdog or safety agent aborted, and does not propose that intensity or a higher one again within the lookback window. An advisory safety agent re-checks the live measurements every few seconds and may abort earlier; it can never cancel a watchdog abort, extend a fault or change a threshold.

Each experiment injects one fault (container crash, added network delay or packet loss), measures every journey during the fault window (up to the abort for aborted runs), reverts the fault, and measures how long the journeys take to return inside the baseline band.

Impact, breadth, recovery and the penalty are computed deterministically from those measurements. The hypothesis verdict compares the journeys the planner predicted would degrade with those that actually did: CONFIRMED when equal, PARTIAL when they overlap, REFUTED when they do not.
A hidden dependency is a journey that degraded by at least 0.3 although neither the hypothesis nor the dependency map expected it.

The analyst agent ranks weaknesses and the fixer agent proposes fixes from the measured results only; their output is validated against known experiments, services and an allowlist of compose keys. When Groq is unavailable or its output is invalid, rule-based fallbacks produce the same sections. Fixes are proposals and are never applied.
